quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Which formation keeps riders closest together in a group?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Single-file formation works better for curves, turns, and entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle into a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn. This makes the motorcycle lean and turn.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes the motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
Is only useful in protecting riders from dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Choose a lane position that fits your riding conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that go above the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of a soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of a soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather or sturdy jacket; boots that cover your ankles; and hearing protection. Soft material pants are not protective.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or put them in saddlebags. Never pile loads high on the back of the seat. This raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers can't see you.
Not worry about making sure other drivers see you.
Ride offensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers can't see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and hard to see compared to other vehicles. Ride defensively and assume other drivers don't see you.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down before hitting an obstacle. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep the motorcycle straight. Just before impact, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Engine braking is:

options.text: Illegal.
Slowing down by turning the engine off.
Slowing down by downshifting.
Not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear creates a braking effect. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Where is the electric starter button usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The electric starter button is located near the right handgrip.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. You will notice a flat tire by how your motorcycle handles, not by sound.

questions.question: A major effect of alcohol consumption is:

options.text: Heightened riding abilities.
The slowing down of bodily functions.
Increasing nervousness.
Increasing alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: The slowing down of bodily functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your body and mind. It makes both physical and mental functions weaker.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through the area as quickly as possible.
Weave between the cars to get through the area as quickly as possible.
Not weave between the cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between the cars.
questions.explanation: Do not weave between cars. Car doors can open suddenly, or cars may pull into traffic without warning. You will have no space to escape if danger appears. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers do not expect motorcycles there.

questions.question: Once a motorcycle helmet has been involved in a crash, it should be:

options.text: Inspected closely.
Replaced.
Sold to another rider.
Outfitted with a new chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Replace your helmet after any crash. A helmet that has been in a crash is no longer safe to use.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: The rear brake should be applied first.
The front brake should be applied first.
Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only one brake, front or rear, should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: Passing and being passed when riding a motorcycle is not much different than when driving a car. However:

options.text: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
A motorcycle's visibility is not as important as that of a car.
Passing should be done on the shoulder instead of on the main roadway.
It is critical to make eye contact with the other driver when riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle's visibility is more critical than that of a car.
questions.explanation: Visibility is more important when riding a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily disappear into a driver's blind spot. Other drivers may not see you even if they are looking.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Has a seat even with the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Has a seat that is 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you are seated. Keep your feet on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure your load so it does not move. This keeps your motorcycle handling stable. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.
